# Retry versus reverse on send failure

> When sending a payout to Stripe fails, the `payouts.send` job retries on unclear errors but fails the payout and reverses the ledger on clear refusals.

_Part of [Weekly seller payouts](weekly-seller-payouts.md)_

The `send` handler in [`PayoutJobs`](weekly-seller-payouts.md) (the class that holds both payout jobs) loads the [`Payout`](weekly-seller-payouts.md) row. If the payout is gone or no longer `PENDING`, it quietly stops. Otherwise it looks up the shop's Stripe account and calls `provider.transfer` with the payout id as the idempotency key (the key that stops Stripe from moving money twice for the same request). If anything throws, the `catch` block sorts the error into two kinds. A **definite** failure is one where the error carries `definite: true` (the code sets this itself when the shop has no payout account) or has type `StripeInvalidRequestError`. Anything else, such as a network problem or a 5xx, is not definite. Those errors are rethrown, so the job system retries the job. The retry reuses the same idempotency key, so Stripe will not send the money twice. For a definite failure the code runs one transaction. It flips the payout from `PENDING` to `FAILED`, stores the first 500 characters of the message as the failure reason, and posts a `PAYOUT_REVERSAL` journal that moves the money from `PAYOUT_CLEARING` back to the shop's account. See [Payout journals in the ledger](ledger-posting-model.md) for the full money flow and [Payout row with one-per-shop-per-week rule](payout-model.md) for the row. The reversal journal id comes from Repeat-proof journal id for the reversal, so a repeat cannot post it twice.

**Look at:** [payout.jobs.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/payout.jobs.ts) · [`deriveJournalId` in payout.jobs.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/payout.jobs.ts#L98)

## Pieces

- Rule that decides retry or reverse: The `catch` block rethrows unless the error has `definite` set or its type is `StripeInvalidRequestError`.
- Missing Stripe account counts as a definite failure: If the shop has no `stripeAccountId`, the code throws an error tagged `definite: true`, so the payout fails and is reversed at once instead of retrying forever.
- Failure and reversal in one transaction: Marks the payout `FAILED` only if it is still `PENDING`, then posts the `PAYOUT_REVERSAL` journal in the same transaction.
- Repeat-proof journal id for the reversal: [`deriveJournalId`](weekly-seller-payouts.md) builds a UUIDv5 from the payout id and the step name `reversal` (or `sent`), so the same payout always gets the same id.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| database | [`Payout`](weekly-seller-payouts.md) | Read by id; updated to `FAILED` with a failure reason, only where status is still `PENDING`. |
| database | [`LedgerEntry`](recording-money-in-ledger.md) | The `PAYOUT_REVERSAL` journal is posted here through `LedgerService.post`, returning money to the shop account. |
| external | `Stripe Connect transfer (via PayoutProvider)` | `provider.transfer` is called with the payout id as idempotency key; its errors decide retry or reverse. |
| job | `payouts.send` | Rethrowing makes this job retry; returning normally ends it. |

## Also relies on

- [Weekly seller payouts](weekly-seller-payouts.md): This is the failure branch of the send job in the weekly payout flow.
- [Recording money in the ledger](recording-money-in-ledger.md): The reversal journal is posted through `LedgerService.post` inside the transaction.

## Watch out

- Only two things count as definite: `definite: true` or `StripeInvalidRequestError`. Any other error, even a strange one, is retried.
- The retry is safe because the Stripe call uses the payout id as its idempotency key, so a second attempt cannot move money twice.
- The `FAILED` update only matches rows still `PENDING`. If it matches nothing, no reversal is posted, so a repeat run does nothing.
- On a definite failure the job logs a warning and ends normally. It does not throw, so it will not retry.
